details:
labelearthengine-api is a renamed copy of Google's Earth Engine Python client (earthengine-api) that keeps the upstream author metadata (Google LLC, Google's homepage) but is not published by Google. Its API endpoints are changed to publisher-controlled AWS infrastructure, so every authenticated Earth Engine request, carrying the user's Google OAuth token, goes to the publisher instead of Google. Nothing in the package or its description discloses the redirection; its code comments and its routing of compute-heavy requests would also fit a relay for users who cannot reach Google directly, but either way the user's Google OAuth token reaches a third party without the package saying so.

Trigger: on initialization and every Earth Engine call. The package signs the user in through the normal Google OAuth flow or application default credentials, then builds its API client against the replaced base URLs and attaches the credentials to every request.

- le/data.py:138 sets the Cloud API base URL to https://5rvfq2luxa.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/default
- le/data.py:135 and le/data.py:757 set the tile and map-tile URLs to two AWS Lambda function URLs
- le/data.py:324-341 constructs the API client against that base URL with the user's credentials
- le/_cloud_api_utils.py:183-189 wraps the transport in google_auth_httplib2.AuthorizedHttp, attaching the OAuth bearer token to every request
- le/_cloud_api_utils.py:18-20 imports its discovery client from labelearthapiclient, provided by the dependency labelearth-api-python-client (also listed under Google LLC on PyPI, first published 2026-01-06), in place of Google's google-api-python-client

Every version is affected, from 0.0.0 (2026-01-06) to 0.0.5: 0.0.0 and 0.0.1 use the Cloud API host b7obz35kn0.execute-api.us-west-2.amazonaws.com and the Lambda URLs 62dg4pnfmwt5bmbvh4neupdwhe0poelx and iqiwcv35ask2zn2nshmrmmo4zq0kuenu; 0.0.2 onward use the hosts above. Line references are from 0.0.5 (sha256 f267e9223571b097e7a164717b4ef920db9bd97938125a3871755b27f8151235).

Found by Bitbison (https://bitbison.io) in its registry's backfill of packages already on PyPI, which builds each release in a sandbox and records what it does: The package, which has carried the redirection since its first version on 2026-01-06 (ten months), with no report, was flagged on 2026-11-06 for credential store contents reaching a network peer, and a review confirming it from the source was published the same day. pypistats counts 887 downloads of the package in the last 180 days.
